title: file-pcapng: Add new field to identify extraneous data
description:
Any data in a pcapng block following an end-of-option option
and the trailer is now identified as 'Extraneous Data'.

notes.body:
The possibility exists that someone might quietly store extraneous data inside of pcapng blocks *after* the end-of-option option.  The MIME based file-pcapng dissector is augmented to report "Extraneous Data".

This behavior was seen in the wild with a pcapng file where all blocks were the same fixed size (some power of 2 like 2^16 (65536), but could have been bigger).  All the blocks were padded with NUL characters. All the extraneous NUL bytes looked to be redundant (but not reported) end-of-option options.

Here is a contrived pcapng file with each block having 4096 octets of extraneous NUL octets.

[extraneous_nuls.pcapng](/uploads/39efd22026ffa116e872cdc6225be5f0/extraneous_nuls.pcapng)

Here is a second silly contrived example of a pcapng file with all the blocks having been padded with 4096 bytes of extraneous data.

[extraneous.pcapng](/uploads/6412a50af3952ca61bd5fc453f692b03/extraneous.pcapng)

In this second example each block's extraneous data is simply a constant ASCII letter, with the first block (the SHB) having extraneous 'A' characters, the 2nd block having extraneous 'B' characters, etc.  There are 23 blocks in total with the last two blocks being EPBs, the first EPB having extraneous 'X' characters and the 2nd EPB having extraneous 'Y' characters.
Shoud we dump the payload using FT_BYTES instead? When using tshark you cannot see what the extraneous data is currently.

I'm also curious whether

https://pocorgtfo.hacke.rs/pocorgtfo21.pdf

has any extraneous data in any blocks.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20257/diffs?diff_id=1395304427&start_sha=637d8b669f60ac3f1e66ef4426fcddeea4203c4e#4709c9292ba8f7813dd2b95269d48dc11eec7894_2176_2176)
@pquantin Yes. Using FT_BYTES results in a much better report.  Done.

Aren't the contents more filterable if they are a traditional item?  But I don't think it hurts to add expert info as well.

Debated with myself regarding the "proper" severity level for the expert info. Opted for PI_NOTE over PI_WARNING (or PI_ERROR). Should we reconsider a "better" severity level?

This expert info has the same filter name as the `FT_BYTES` item created in the previous commit. That confuses the filter engine a bit (an expert info item is a `FT_NONE`). Some of the CI builds will show a warning, e.g., https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/10657328629#L3246 (if `-DENABLE_CHECKHF_CONFLICT=on` is given).

Thanks for the heads-up. I'll submit an MR to change the expert info filter name.

There appears to be a disambiguation precedent of making an ht_xxx_yyy_zzz filter name unique from an ei_xxx_yyy_zzz filter by changing one of the "." characters to an "_" character or visa-versa.
